source_text: Inimicos suos dicta nostra in veritatis odium suscepisse et toto penitus Occidente non minus stultum quam impium dogma esse susceptum et simplicibus episcopis sine congregatione synodi in locis suis manentibus subscriptiones extortas
pass_a_gloss: that their enemies have taken up our statements into hatred of the truth, and that throughout the whole West a teaching no less foolish than ungodly has been taken up, and that from simple bishops remaining in their own places, without a synod being gathered, signatures have been extorted
pass_b_english: Their enemies have adopted Augustine’s statements out of hatred for the truth. Throughout the entire West, a doctrine as foolish as it is impious has been accepted. Signatures confirming it have been extorted from unsuspecting bishops who remained in their own places, without a synod being assembled.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian and fellow bishops (Collective letter to Thessalonica, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 2–4); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
